narr: A large area of strong to severe thunderstorms moving across Central Texas early on May 5th gradually shifted into parts of East Texas shortly after daybreak. Although the overall risk of severe thunderstorms had decreased given a relative lack of instability, stronger and organized updrafts persisted locally. The most significant thunderstorms were long-lived, rotating clusters moving into East Texas, where several reports of damaging winds were documented in Angelina County along with a few reports of flash flooding in Smith County. Later in the afternoon and early evening, additional thunderstorms redeveloped with one isolated severe storm producing quarter size hail in the city of Marshall in Harrison County.
